title: FIFA defends Infantino against 'concerted effort' to oust him
dek: FIFA issued a formal statement defending president Gianni Infantino against what it called a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to undermine the organization, following Daily Telegraph allegations and escalating pressure from UEFA over a failed commercial restructuring proposal. Infantino denies the allegations. Global confederation blocs backing Infantino stand against European opposition.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: FIFA stated Infantino was 'democratically elected by FIFA's Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate,' while UEFA has declared it has lost confidence in him and maintains a threat to boycott FIFA events.
bottom_line: The conflict now hinges on whether FIFA's claim of democratic mandate outweighs UEFA's loss of confidence and threatened boycott. Watch for whether UEFA receives formal assurances on the FFE proposal or escalates its boycott threat, and whether the bloc of non-European confederations can sustain unified backing for Infantino if the institutional challenge persists.
body: FIFA has mounted a formal defense of president Gianni Infantino against what it characterized as a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to undermine the organization, according to BBC Sport. The statement comes after the Daily Telegraph reported allegations about Infantino's personal conduct, including claims about a severance payment made by UEFA to an alleged lover after Infantino's tenure as the body's general secretary. A FIFA spokesperson told the Telegraph that Infantino 'strongly denies' the allegations and that they are 'categorically untrue'.

The conflict extends beyond personal disputes into institutional governance. Infantino has faced escalating pressure from UEFA and European football associations over his proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a commercial restructuring that would have created a new company to manage commercial and ticketing rights, with 21 percent sold to a private investment company. UEFA has stated it has lost confidence in Infantino and maintains a threat to boycott FIFA events, per BBC Sport. The Norwegian Football Federation president called for Infantino's resignation, and UEFA says it has not received assurances that the FFE plan cannot be revived.

In its statement, per BBC Sport, FIFA rejected what it called 'unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims,' adding that 'speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact.' The organization emphasized that Infantino 'was democratically elected by FIFA's Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.' FIFA further stated: 'Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.'

Opposition to Infantino is largely confined to Europe. The Mexican Football Federation broke ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to support Infantino, according to BBC Sport. Conmebol, South America's governing body, said it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 FIFA member countries. Infantino is unanimously backed by the 54 nations of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), per BBC Sport.
